around.headline: TTP-linked man arrested in Bengaluru over planned attack on Pakistan Army, two more held nearby
around.summary: Bengaluru police arrested a man with alleged links to Pakistan-based terror outfit TTP over a planned attack on the Pakistan Army, with a security guard and two others held in a related case in Kalaburagi, ahead of today's high-security Independence Day. Expect visible extra checks and barricades around Independence Day events and transit hubs through the day.
around.source: The Times of India, The New Indian Express

around.headline: Bengalurean loses Rs 1 crore in a year chasing trading losses; 'trading academy' video triggers separate case
around.summary: A Bengaluru resident who started trading with Rs 10 lakh lost Rs 1 crore over a year by repeatedly adding money to recover earlier losses, while a separate 'trading academy' promotion has triggered its own police case in the city. If a trading tip group or academy promises one more top-up will recoup everything you've lost, that promise is the trap — verify SEBI registration before adding another rupee.

around.headline: Dog dispute turns violent, woman assaulted in Bengaluru
around.summary: A dispute over a dog escalated into a physical assault on a woman in the city. As with any street altercation, creating distance and pulling in bystanders or police (100) is safer than engaging directly.

around.headline: Freedom Habba draws 18,000+ registrations for Independence Day, with traffic curbs and Metro closure
around.summary: Bengaluru's first Independence Day "Freedom Habba" at Vidhana Soudha has over 18,000 registered, and comes with traffic curbs, a nearby Metro station closure and QR-code entry, alongside elaborate citywide security arrangements today. Check your route in advance and carry your registration QR if you're headed there.

around.headline: On-street parking permit rules spark backlash over cost, fears of higher rent
around.summary: Draft rules charging Rs 10-80/hour (up to Rs 25,000/year) for on-street parking outside homes have drawn backlash, with citizens saying public transport and last-mile links should improve first — and some fear landlords will pass the cost on as higher rent. Worth watching if you currently park on the street regularly.

around.headline: Expired maida, stale bread found in Bengaluru hospital kitchen amid wider food-safety gaps
around.summary: A Bengaluru hospital kitchen was found with expired maida and stale bread, part of a wider pattern of food-safety gaps found this week from star hotels to quick-commerce warehouses. If you or family are hospitalised, it's reasonable to ask about food sourcing or bring outside meals where possible.

around.summary: India marked its 80th Independence Day today, with PM Modi addressing the nation from the Red Fort, and elaborate security bandobast in place across Bengaluru as well. street_smart.title: A friend who's been trading online tells you he's down Rs 1 crore over the past year — after starting with just Rs 10 lakh — chasing recovery on each previous loss, echoing today's news of a Bengalurean who lost exactly that. He says one more top-up to a 'trading academy' group will finally turn it around. What do you tell him?
street_smart.based_on: Today's real Bengaluru news: a city resident who started trading with Rs 10 lakh lost Rs 1 crore over a year chasing losses, and a separate 'trading academy' promotion triggered a police case (The Times of India).
street_smart.situation: Your friend joined a paid 'trading academy'/tips group after a small initial loss. Screenshots of other members' huge profits keep circulating in the group, and the admin says a bigger top-up now will help recoup everything he's lost so far.

choices.text: Tell him to stop adding any more money right now, treat what's already gone as a sunk cost, and check the platform's/advisor's SEBI registration at sebi.gov.in before anyone puts in another rupee.
choices.feedback: Correct. 'One more top-up to recover it all' is the exact trap — legitimate SEBI-registered advisors don't guarantee returns or ask you to chase losses; verifying registration first is how you catch an unregistered scheme before it takes more.

choices.text: Help him find the extra money for the top-up, since the group's previous 'profit' screenshots looked real and a few members did get earlier payouts.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Scammers often let early, small withdrawals go through specifically to build trust — the sunk-cost feeling of having already lost so much is what makes the bigger, final ask work; real trading losses don't get recovered by putting more money with the same people.

choices.text: Tell him to just quietly walk away and never mention the group to anyone, without reporting it anywhere.
choices.feedback: Risky. Walking away is right, but staying silent means the operators keep running the same script on others — filing a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in or calling 1930 costs a few minutes and can help freeze transferred funds and shut the operation down.

choices.text: Suggest he demand his money back directly from the group admin before doing anything else.
choices.feedback: Risky. Confronting the operators alone rarely gets money back and can tip them off to disappear or delete evidence — report to the National Cyber Crime helpline first so there's an official trail, then let authorities pursue recovery.

takeaways: Never add more money to 'recover' a trading loss — chasing losses with the same platform or group is the exact psychological hook scammers rely on.
Check any trading advisor, academy, or platform's SEBI registration at sebi.gov.in before investing — legitimate advisors never guarantee returns.
Report suspected investment fraud immediately to the National Cyber Crime helpline 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in — early reporting improves the odds of freezing transferred funds.

quiz.question: Bengaluru's new draft on-street parking rules could charge residents up to how much per year to park outside their own home?
quiz.why: The hourly rate is proposed at Rs 10-80/hour, and citizens say public transport and last-mile links should improve before the fees kick in.

quiz.question: Which August 15 Bengaluru event at Vidhana Soudha has drawn over 18,000 registrations, with traffic curbs and a Metro station closure?
quiz.why: It's Bengaluru's first Independence Day mega-festival, with a parade, art installations, building tours and QR-code entry for registered visitors.

quiz.question: India marked its 80th Independence Day today, with PM Modi addressing the nation from the Red Fort. In what year did India actually gain independence?
quiz.why: 1950 is when the Constitution came into force and India became a republic — a separate milestone celebrated on Republic Day (January 26), not Independence Day.

quiz.question: What is the minimum age at which an Indian citizen becomes eligible to vote?
quiz.why: The voting age was lowered from 21 to 18 by the 61st Constitutional Amendment in 1988.

quiz.question: Bengaluru's name is popularly linked to a legend about a lost 12th-century king being served 'benda kaalu' by an old woman. What does that Kannada phrase mean?
quiz.why: The spot where he was fed is said to have become known as 'benda-kaal-uru' — 'town of boiled beans' — which evolved into the name Bengaluru.
